title: Apple Music adapter diagnostics and FairPlay flag handling match the legacy path RF-124 restored
acceptance: The playback-failed banner no longer appends a modern-access probe word that describes a path MusicKit does not use.
The unprefixed com.apple.fps probe no longer runs in play() on iOS, or a measured reason to keep it is recorded (coordinate with RF-128).

The stored mk-safari-modern-eme flag is cleared once at MusicKit load instead of at four call sites, and the flag log runs after the key session attaches, with accurate comments (including FAIRPLAY_KEY_SYSTEM).
The desktop test asserts only that the FairPlay key is not removed, not that no removeItem call happens.
Owner hears Start, Next and auto-advance in iPhone Safari Live after the change (provider code, CI cannot prove it).

The #664 review items 1, 3, 4 and 5 are handled under RF-108's lock and supersession design, which must pass these checks: a timed-out setQueue generation is superseded; nowPlayingItem is checked before play, so a late settle cannot play the old song; a setQueue that settles after its timeout cannot start the old song; setQueue uses one try/finally; and a test covers a late settle and the not-destroyed path. The PR that lands RF-108's design meets this criterion.
nextAction: After PR #668 merges and deploys, the owner hears Start, Next and auto-advance in iPhone Safari Live (the same run as RF-108's device check). When RF-108 is Done and that run passes, move this to Done.
blocker: Code for criteria 0-3 and 5 is in PR #668. Criterion 4 is the owner's iPhone Safari check, and this task now depends on RF-108 (owner of the setQueue/play lock design), which closes only after its own iPhone device check.

evidence.summary: Final review of #657: no significant findings; nine non-blocking findings. Item 1 (MusicKit re-writing the flag) is answered by the owner's passing iPhone runs; item 2 (desktop Safari legacy path) is in RF-126.
Final review of #664 (RF-123): no significant findings; logged items 1, 3, 4 and 5 are adapter hardening and cleanup in apple-music-adapter.ts setQueue().
Owner set Ready in session on 2026-10-30 ("Yes, option 1, Apple hardening"): RF-108, RF-128 and RF-147 as one Apple hardening lane.

Banner is now "Apple Music playback failed for "<title>"." with the probe word logged to the console; play() no longer calls the com.apple.fps probe on iOS Safari (no timing measured, so no reason to keep it was recorded; legacy desktop WebKit keeps it as a console diagnostic); the mk-safari-modern-eme flag is cleared once per page in loadMusicKit and logged once after MusicKit's first play() resolves; FAIRPLAY_KEY_SYSTEM and flag comments corrected; desktop Chrome test asserts only that the FairPlay key is not removed. The RF-108 lease design supersedes a timed-out generation, checks nowPlayingItem and a late-settle count before play, and uses one try/finally in setQueue.

"supersedes a timed-out setQueue generation, so its late settle cannot play the old song (RF-147)" (not-destroyed path), "a cancelled queue request that settles after its successor cued is re-cued over before play" (destroyed path), and "checks nowPlayingItem before play and re-cues only when it names another song"; musickit.test.ts covers the once-per-page clear and flag log. Mock MusicKit only.

Commit 05ad7ea (#668 review fixes): the iOS rule now lives inside probeSafariModernFairPlayAccess, which returns null on iOS Safari with or without WebKitMediaKeys; the desktop Chrome test was restored to assert removeItem is never called (review finding 10), which differs from criterion 3's wording.

Commit fe6a1d1: the late-settle guarantee for criterion 5 is now: before play, play() re-cues over a late settle; after start, a late settle that replaced the song shows Retry (never auto-plays). fairPlayFlagCleared resets with the probe test helper; the flag is still cleared once per page (the owner's passing runs before RF-147 cleared it per call; the device run checks song 2+).

Owner ruling in session 2026-10-30 ("The stricter testing is acceptable"), recorded in the #668 comment that applied owner-approved on 6595d3f: the desktop Chrome test asserting removeItem is never called meets criterion 3.
